title: Stress driver for streaming chat: high-concurrency SSE & WebSocket load harness
creator: Ari Patel
description: Build a robust, configurable stress driver that can emulate real streaming chat/completion traffic over both server-sent events (SSE) and WebSocket transports. The harness must exercise the full serving stack (frontend balancers, routing policies, runtime instances) and produce reproducible tokens/sec and p95 latency profiles with automated regression detection and tagging for failed runs.
goals: Create a production-like load generator capable of maintaining sustained token throughput and connection churn at scale (target 1M tokens/min simulated across cluster).
Measure p50/p95/p99 generation latency end-to-end per message chunk, and per-token throughput (tokens/sec) per model shard and per customer route.
Detect regressions automatically: baseline runs + weekly scheduled runs with statistical comparison and alerting (delta thresholds configurable).
Support scenarios: cold KV cache vs warmed cache, variable sequence lengths, function/tool calls (structured events), and bursty conversational traffic with reconnects and backpressure handling.
success_criteria: Harness can sustain 10k concurrent streaming connections (mix of SSE and WebSocket) while generating 1M tokens/min in staging without client-side errors >0.5%.
Automated run produces a single CSV/JSON summary including tokens/sec, p95 latency, connection churn, retry counts, and per-instance resource utilization for easy diffing against baseline.
Regression detection pipeline flags >=2% regression in p95 or >=5% drop in tokens/sec vs baseline and files an alert with attached artifacts (trace ids, example sessions, sample traces).
Instrumentation added so each simulated session includes trace headers and request tags to link with Console dashboards and traces.
design_notes: Use a custom Go-based driver for control over concurrency, low-latency network IO, and precise token-rate shaping. k6/wrk can't accurately simulate streaming chunk semantics or long-lived connections at this scale.
Driver will support both text/event-stream SSE and binary/text WebSocket protocols; abstraction layer for chunk framing so tests can reuse conversation scenarios across transports.
Session state: harness must model client-side prompt priming, incremental user messages, and client-driven aborts/reconnects to exercise KV cache warm/cold behaviors.
Tokenization: use the same tokenizer library as runtime to compute token counts for rate limiting and to report tokens/sec accurately.
workload_profiles: Steady conversational: 10k concurrent sessions, avg 3 messages/session/min, avg response length 120 tokens (mix short/long tails).
Bursty sessions: 2k sessions that send 10 messages within 30s bursts to test autoscaling and batching thresholds.
Cold-cache ramp: sequentially spin up new sessions across model shards to measure first-request penalty and KV cache population time.
Function-calling pattern: 20% of responses include structured function/tool calls requiring additional round-trip and payload parsing.
metrics_to_capture: tokens_sec_cluster: aggregated tokens/sec generated by the cluster
end_to_end_response_ms: time from first client request to final chunk received
connection_success_rate_pct: percentage of connections established vs attempted
cpu_gpu_utilization_per_instance: infra-level metrics to correlate saturation
kv_cache_hit_rate: proportion of requests served from warmed KV cache
failure_modes_and_tests: Backpressure: simulate slow client consumers to ensure server streaming respects buffering limits and that memory doesn't blow up. Test by throttling read on client sockets.
Partial chunk loss: inject network packet drops and verify session reconnection logic and idempotency of resumed streams.
Autoscaler reaction: abruptly double load to verify Dedicated autoscaling and verify fallback policies (route to hosted variants) kick in within SLO.
Model regression: use baseline sample prompts and compare sampling token distributions; detect silent quality regressions by token timing anomalies and token production rates.
TLS/handshake failures: randomize will-fail handshake rate to ensure driver surfaces meaningful errors for debugging.
harness_architecture: Controller service (Go) that orchestrates test runs, schedules client workers, and collects metrics via Prometheus pushgateway.
Client worker pool (Go) that maintains N long-lived connections; each worker can host thousands of virtual sessions using epoll/async io.
Scenario library as JSONL artifacts (no nested schemas) describing conversation seeds, expected chunk shapes, and optional assertions for content structure.
Results collector that emits run artifacts: per-session traces (sampled), aggregate CSV summary, and raw event logs for replaying failed sessions.
Integration hooks: push metrics to staging Prometheus, emit traces to Jaeger, and upload artifacts to an S3 test-bucket for long-term storage.
infra_requirements: Staging cluster with capacity to run load generator pods on separate nodes (isolate CPU network from runtime cluster).
Dedicated Prometheus + Grafana dashboard for load runs.
Provisioned model-serving pool in staging with representative model (quantized, full-precision variants) and sharding configuration matching production.
S3 bucket and retention policy for run artifacts; pre-signed URLs for large logs.
dashboards_and_alerts: Load-run summary dashboard: tokens/sec, p95 chunk latency, connection churn, errors, per-instance throughput.
Regression alert: triggered when p95 increases by >2% and tokens/sec drops >5% vs baseline OR when connection_success_rate < 99% during a run.
Resource saturation alerts tied to test runs: GPU utilization >90% for >2 minutes should be captured but not auto-escalated if expected by the run plan.
test_schedule: Phase 1 (week 1): implement driver core, SSE and WebSocket transports, and small-scale sanity runs (100-500 sessions).
Phase 2 (week 2): medium scale validation (5k-20k concurrent sessions), add token counting and CSV summary output.
Phase 3 (week 3): full-scale runs (10k+ concurrent), regression pipeline integration, dashboarding, and alert tuning.
Ongoing: scheduled weekly baseline runs with automated diffing and a human-in-loop triage workflow for flagged regressions.
